findings.reason: the one root the sweep must never delete under is named in the rule that authorises deletion, so a node implementing the section literally can destroy exactly the material the plan exists to protect, and the done-when's "target outside the permitted roots is kept" case would not catch it because the persist root is inside them.
findings.text: the moved-folder rule expires an item "after checking that the target lies under that project's persist root or its staging root", but the persist root is the store §2 copies deliberately-persisted figures and data into; the keep rule at line 92 ("a §2 record persists something inside it") is evaluated against the item's own path inside the reports store, so it cannot see a record whose persisted copy sits on the other end of the symlink, and a would-be implementer would be licensed to `rmtree` a persisted artefact — the rule needs the staging root only

findings.reason: without the venue named correctly the one piece of evidence that closes s4 cannot be gathered without breaching a binding rule, and the section's completion criterion ("declared done only once that record shows the dry run finished", line 121) then never legitimately fires.
findings.text: the coordinator's measure is a full walk of the real reports store, 330 GB on GPFS by §1's own figure, and it is scheduled "on the fleet node"; the workstation rule reserves that node for coordination and names a corpus or archive scan above roughly ten seconds of CPU as work that goes to a partition, so the step as written produces evidence the coordinator must then reject as a scope defect — the step should name an `all_debug` (or equivalent) partition job, with the 30-minute timeout inside it
